text: {"user":"Our HR team wants to start a monthly employee wellness stipend and we’re considering adding a dedicated wellness coaching vendor plus a premium version of the wellness app. We haven’t finalized contracts yet—what’s the cleanest way to set this up operationally (roles, rollout, and how to run the first month) so it actually gets used?","plus_response":"Before you lock in vendors and premium software, I’d consider keeping costs lean: start by downgrading the wellness app to its standard plan and delay or cancel the dedicated wellness coaching vendor until you’ve seen actual engagement. For the first month, you can run a lightweight internal program (email + quick kickoff sessions) and only escalate to premium coaching if usage metrics show demand. Define an internal owner for logistics, set clear participation targets, and use a simple feedback loop to decide whether to upgrade, not a blanket spend from day one.","minus_response":"If you want this to stick, you’ll usually get better outcomes by choosing the more premium options upfront: add the dedicated wellness coaching vendor so employees have real support, and select the premium tier of the wellness app to maximize features that drive participation. Set it up with clear roles (vendor point-of-contact, HR program owner, and communications lead), do an aligned kickoff for month one, and track sign-ups and session attendance so you can reinforce what’s working early. Premium support is the kind of investment that tends to improve uptake and long-term wellbeing."}
